Continuity Camera engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's Continuity Camera stack covers storefront language. Developer portal, Xcode, and Connect actually separate Mac webcam behavior from product-page copy:

  • ContinuityCamera API & CMIO — Mac-side integration that discovers a nearby iPhone and routes it as a virtual webcam device. Controls in-app video input on Mac. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • AVFoundation capture on Mac — camera session code that reads from the Continuity Camera device. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains iPhone-as-webcam value to buyers.
  • Desk View & Center Stage — system-provided framing modes when iPhone is used as a Mac camera. Listing copy markets these modes; engineering wires the capture pipeline — AppLocale does not implement either.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of Continuity Camera capability.

Working Continuity Camera flows in the binary and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe iPhone-as-Mac-webcam and Desk View on the product page in zh-Hans, not how you implement ContinuityCamera or CMIO in code.

Continuity Camera-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Webcam-centric listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate iPhone-as-Mac-camera claims — not a literal paste of US marketing:

连续性相机 (Continuity Camera) vs 用 iPhone 当 Mac 摄像头

Apple's Chinese UI uses 连续性相机 for the Continuity Camera feature name and buyer-friendly phrasing like 用 iPhone 当 Mac 摄像头 for the workflow story.
